<description>
When checking whether a gateway replied with NAT-PMP unsupported version (RFC 6887 appendix A and RFC 6886 section 3.5), `PCPRequestPortMap` mistakenly used `PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS` (3) and compared only a single byte against `NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION`.

NAT-PMP result codes are 16-bit big-endian values starting at offset 2 (`NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS`). A 16-bit result code with low byte 1 and a non-zero high byte (such as `0x0101`) would previously be incorrectly treated as `UNSUPP_VERSION`.

This PR fixes the check to use `ReadBE16(response.data() + NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS)` matching the rest of `pcp.cpp` (lines 348 and 390), and uses `NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS` for the version field offset. A unit test is added to `pcp_tests.cpp`.
</description>

<commits>
aa57403920 net: parse NAT-PMP result code as 16-bit BE in PCP fallback

When checking whether a gateway replied with NAT-PMP unsupported version (RFC 6887 appendix A and RFC 6886 section 3.5), PCPRequestPortMap mistakenly used PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS (3) and compared only a single byte against NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION.

NAT-PMP result codes are 16-bit big-endian values starting at offset 2 (NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS). A 16-bit result code with low byte 1 and a non-zero high byte (such as 0x0101) would previously be incorrectly treated as UNSUPP_VERSION.

Use ReadBE16 with NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS instead, matching the rest of pcp.cpp, and use NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS for the version check. Add a unit test covering this case.
